evidence: Two links, both re-run by verify_qin_2025_behavioral_intention.R. (1) code->column: live table joined to the study's S1 Data CSV on id=='No.', 547/547 respondents; each live item agrees with the source column of the same name on 100.0% of respondents (547/547 for BI1, BI2 and BI3) and with the other two BI columns on only 57.2%/58.1% (BI1), 57.2%/64.7% (BI2), 58.1%/64.7% (BI3) -- every item is distinguished from every other, and no permutation of the three codes reproduces the live data. (2) column->paper code: the paper's Table 7 cross-loadings for BI1/BI2/BI3 on CI, PCD, RCTE, SA (0.728/0.258/0.764/0.821; 0.680/0.242/0.687/0.765; 0.688/0.235/0.703/0.781) are reproduced from the S1 Data columns as 0.728/0.254/0.763/0.820, 0.680/0.240/0.687/0.765, 0.688/0.233/0.703/0.781 -- 12/12 cells, largest residual 0.0041; swapping BI2 and BI3 raises the worst residual to 0.0164 (4.1x) and all four published BI3-BI2 gaps (+0.008, -0.007, +0.016, +0.016) are reproduced with the correct sign. What this does NOT establish: neither link reads the wording itself -- the words come from S1 Table, which prints the codes BI1/BI2/BI3 beside the three sentences (Step 5b's explicit-code-label exemption); and the BI2-vs-BI3 separation in link (2) rests on gaps of 0.008-0.016, small absolutely though 2-4x the observed residual, with link (1) carrying that pair on its own.
